course_metadata.institution: University at Albany, State University of New York
course_metadata.prerequisites: No prerequisite; general mathematical knowledge and computer skills are recommended.
course_metadata.credit_exclusion: Only one of IECE 200, IECE 141, and IECE/ICSI 201 may be taken for credit.

grade_scale.C: 73-76% (Minimum required for S grade under S/U option)

grading_scheme.negotiation_policy: Final grades are strictly non-negotiable per department policy. Students may not submit extra work or be re-examined after completion of the course.

course_policies.late_submission_policy: Work submitted within 24 hours after the deadline is considered late and receives an automatic 50% grade reduction. No submissions are accepted after this 24-hour window.
zero_credit_conditions: Work is not submitted through the learning management platform (Brightspace).
Work is submitted past the 24-hour late cutoff window.
Work is improperly submitted (blurry, corrupted files, missing required documents, or incorrect formats).
Work is copied partially or fully from peers, previous students, or online sources.
course_policies.grade_disputes: Students have a strictly limited dispute window after grades are posted. Inquiries must be sent by email to the assigned grader with specific justifications. Late disputes are disregarded.
course_policies.makeup_exam_policy: Make-up exams are granted only for verified urgent emergencies (e.g., medical illness, accident). Students must notify within 24 hours and provide official documentation. Approved make-ups must be taken before the next class meeting.

attendance_and_participation.tracking_method: iClicker app required on phone or laptop for lectures and labs.
attendance_and_participation.dispute_window: Any attendance discrepancy must be resolved by the end of that same class meeting day.

course_policies.classroom_regulations: Cell phones and other electronics must be turned off. Laptops are strictly restricted to note-taking only.

academic_integrity.collaboration_rules: Students may verbally discuss problem concepts, but all submitted work, code, and documents must be original and written entirely individually.

penalties.first_offense: Automatic grade of zero on the assignment for both the student who copied and the student who shared work.
penalties.repeat_offense: Automatic failing grade of 'E' for the entire course.
penalties.official_action: Violations are formally documented via a Violation of Academic Integrity Report (VAIR) to the CS Department Chair, College Dean, and Vice Provost. Multiple violations lead to expulsion.

toolchain_and_software.programming_language: Java (Java SE Development Kit / JDK 17 or JDK 21)
toolchain_and_software.course_platform: Brightspace (Primary hub for submissions, announcements, and grades)
toolchain_and_software.backup_mandate: Students are required to keep daily local backups on portable drives. Hardware failures or crashed drives are explicitly rejected as valid excuses for late submissions.

course_schedule.topic: Decision Structures & Introduction to Loops and Files
